Each component resets the shared formatter, validates asynchronously, and may append failures. Cascade-stop must restore state before leaving the element loop; dependent rules depend on the whole collection's failure-count baseline rather than only the current element.

Component conditions are evaluated against root context before the collection is fetched, using a copied validator list. Sync-generated execution also has explicit guards against asynchronous conditions, creating a second execution contract to preserve.

primary.counterevidence: This is a thin adapter with one explicit context mutation and no local path processing, iteration, error recovery or lifecycle coordination. The complexity of provider operations is not established by this file.
primary.inspection_scope: Read all 76 source lines. Did not inspect ContentCommandBase or CmdletProviderContext creation and do not assume their ownership behavior beyond what is visible here.

primary.role: COM HRESULT constants and success predicate
primary.hardest_behavior: The only executable behavior tests whether a signed HRESULT is nonnegative; other members declare fixed bit-pattern constants.

evidence.reason: HRESULT values are constants, with unchecked integer casts explicitly retaining hexadecimal bit patterns.
IsSuccess is the single expression hresult >= 0, without state, conversion chains or interacting cases.

primary.counterevidence: An edit still needs the intended COM value or sign convention checked, but this is a direct constant/predicate review. Caller complexity cannot be inferred from the list of error codes.
primary.inspection_scope: Read all 36 source lines. Did not inspect HRESULT callers or external COM specifications.

secondary.role: COM HRESULT constants and success classifier.
secondary.hardest_behavior: Interpreting HRESULT values as signed integers, with success defined by a nonnegative value.

evidence.reason: The error constants explicitly preserve their hexadecimal bit patterns via unchecked casts to int.
The only executable operation is the direct hresult >= 0 predicate; no mutable state or dependent decisions are present.

secondary.counterevidence: An altered value or sign convention would change callers' classification, so constants should be checked against their intended definitions. This is a localized declarative check, not evidence of interacting behavior.
secondary.inspection_scope: Read all 36 lines. Did not inspect COM callers or externally verify constant values.

primary.role: Roslyn editorconfig option and diagnostic-severity updater
primary.hardest_behavior: Changing rule placement or replacement requires simultaneously preserving configuration-kind semantics, matching the diagnostic path and language to sections, last-entry precedence, comment/whitespace retention, and sequential immutable-solution updates. Existing option severity suffixes and build-visible diagnostic severity entries intentionally follow different insertion rules.

evidence.reason: Code-style updates thread a current Project through multiple solution snapshots; severity changes update existing option entries and then independently ensure a diagnostic severity entry exists, with language scope aggregated across options.
Global configuration detection changes header state; replacement is allowed only under the current valid header and preserves option value or severity suffix depending on configuration kind.
Relative-path matching, filename protection, compiler/per-language distinction and the no-source-location case drive separate valid-section and preferred-section spans used later for insertion.
Only the last candidate text change is applied for duplicate entries, so traversal order is semantic rather than incidental.

Missing entries prefer a language-specific valid section, fall back to another valid section, or synthesize a language header; newline placement and section scope must remain consistent with the earlier search.

primary.counterevidence: The implementation documents its precedence choices, uses immutable SourceText changes, and separates entry creation from searching. Those aids make the behavior inspectable, but do not remove the interactions among stateful section tracking, entry forms and solution evolution.
primary.inspection_scope: Read all 774 source lines, including public configuration entry points, project/document creation, option mapping, full section search and insertion. Did not inspect other partial-class files or dependent path/configuration services.

primary.role: C# syntax-name simplification with semantic and syntax-context preservation.
primary.hardest_behavior: Selecting an alias, predefined type, nullable form, shortened qualified name, or attribute name while preserving binding, legal parsing, annotations, trivia, and the diagnostic span; applicability depends on enclosing syntax and semantic resolution.

evidence.reason: Alias replacement preserves source escaping and copies token/node annotations, adjusts the unnecessary span, and may then remove Attribute only after additional context and semantic checks.
Nullable rewriting must replace the whole qualified type and can fall back to qualification reduction if that replacement is invalid.
For cref names, correctness of reducing a child can depend on binding the enclosing qualified reference, so verification is deliberately lifted to the parent.
Nullable applicability distinguishes nameof, unbound generics, cref member form, metadata types, and type arguments declared inside the reference itself.
Speculative semantic equivalence and syntax-context checks are separate gates; several earlier replacement paths call only the context gate, making the choice of validation path substantive.
A replacement is reparsed to catch a cast becoming an arithmetic expression, showing why symbol agreement alone is insufficient.

primary.counterevidence: Immutable syntax construction, named validation helpers, and worked examples make individual rules readable. The semantic speculation helper centralizes a major check. The challenge is preserving the combined applicability and ordering of these rules, not understanding each small helper alone.
primary.inspection_scope: Read all 737 lines. Traced replacement construction and local validation paths; did not inspect SpeculationAnalyzer, inherited simplification helpers, or execute compiler tests.

primary.role: Razor document intermediate-representation node, including replay/cloning state.
primary.hardest_behavior: Cloning a document while sharing already-lowered declaration subtrees and preserving the distinction between a pre-compilation shell, a fallback discovery declaration, and the fallback component name.

evidence.reason: The two declaration properties have different roles for fully split versus fallback components; a fallback name routes discovery independently of the presence of a declaration shell.

CloneNode intentionally aliases both declaration subtrees on the assertion that they are already lowered and inert during replay, while preserving discovery metadata, options, and target. Changing ownership or lifecycle requires checking that assumption.

primary.counterevidence: Most members are passive properties and visitor/formatter forwarding. The ownership exception is explicitly documented, and the base class handles common state and child cloning. No phase orchestration is implemented here.
primary.inspection_scope: Read all 88 lines and IntermediateNode.cs lines 85-115, confirming the base deep-clones Children separately. Did not trace the splitting/lowering phases or generator consumers; confidence in the cross-phase lifetime assumption is limited to the source contract.

primary.role: Remote process telemetry initialization and service-owned performance reporter lifecycle.
primary.hardest_behavior: Changing initialization or disposal requires preserving the different lifetimes of the started telemetry session, process-global fault sink, and service-owned reporter. Reporter creation also subscribes to another service's events and starts deferred work, so its lifetime is more than a field assignment.

evidence.reason: The RPC starts the telemetry session, initializes the workspace telemetry service, and installs a fault sink explicitly retained for the remote process lifetime. Ordering and ownership span multiple services.
An optional performance tracker controls reporter construction with the same telemetry session. The reporter dependency subscribes to SnapshotAdded and owns an asynchronous batching queue.
Service disposal tears down the reporter before base disposal, while the process fault sink intentionally follows a different lifetime.

primary.counterevidence: The local sequence is short and explicit, the optional dependency has a simple guard, and reporting details are encapsulated in the reporter. There is no evidence here of an existing lifecycle defect or urgent problem.
primary.inspection_scope: Read all 71 lines. Also read RemoteProcessTelemetryService.PerformanceReporter.cs and RemoteWorkspaceTelemetryService.cs for event subscription, queue ownership, and telemetry service context. Did not inspect the base RPC implementation or exercise initialization/disposal.
